subtitle: Prafulla Chandra Ray and the Birth of Swadeshi Chemistry

panels.shot: epic mid-shot in a dim home laboratory, shelves of glass bottles and crude apparatus glowing in lamplight
panels.action: Prafulla Chandra Ray stands in a cramped Calcutta room turned laboratory, hand resting on a battered balance, eyes steady as rows of labelled reagents catch the warm light.

dialogue.text: In an age of foreign factories and imported pills, Prafulla Chandra Ray returns from Edinburgh and dares to build swadeshi science—and industry—from a few rented rooms in Calcutta.

i18n.hi: विदेशी कारखानों और आयात की गोलियों के दौर में, एडिनबरा से लौटे प्रफुल्ल चंद्र राय कलकत्ता के कुछ किराए के कमरों से स्वदेशी विज्ञान और उद्योग खड़ा करने की हिम्मत करते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Ray writing at a desk, Edinburgh diploma and Bengali books around him
panels.action: In a modest Calcutta study, Ray sits at a wooden desk, Edinburgh certificates on one wall and dog-eared Bengali and Sanskrit volumes piled on the other, pen poised over a notebook.

dialogue.text: He has tasted the laboratories of Edinburgh, won degrees and medals, yet he chooses to return home—to Presidency College—where Indian students wait and the research tables are bare.

i18n.hi: वह एडिनबरा की प्रयोगशालाएँ देख चुका है, डिग्री और मेडल जीत चुका है, फिर भी वह घर लौटना चुनता है—प्रेसीडेंसी कॉलेज—जहाँ भारतीय छात्र इंतज़ार में हैं और शोध की मेज़ें खाली पड़ी हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a stark Presidency College lab, long benches, few instruments, students in the background
panels.action: Ray stands at the front of a sparse chemistry laboratory at Presidency College, simple benches and a handful of glassware between scattered students in coarse cotton clothes.

dialogue.text: Presidency College offers him a platform but little equipment. British rule has built universities, not Indian industries. Chemistry is taught, seldom used to forge livelihoods.

i18n.hi: प्रेसीडेंसी कॉलेज उसे मंच देता है, साधन नहीं। फिरंगी हुकूमत ने विश्वविद्यालय बनाए, भारतीय उद्योग नहीं। रसायन पढ़ाया जाता है, रोज़गार गढ़ने में कम ही लगाया जाता है।

panels.shot: close-up on Ray’s hands arranging retorts and flasks in a cramped corner room
panels.action: In a narrow rented room, Ray leans over a rough table, carefully arranging retorts, flasks and a spirit lamp, his face lit by the small blue flame.

dialogue.text: So he makes his own laboratory at home. The room is small, the glassware cheap, but for Ray each bubbling flask is a promise that serious research can live on Indian soil.

i18n.hi: तो वह घर पर ही अपनी लैब बना लेता है। कमरा छोटा, काँच के बरतन सस्ते, लेकिन राय के लिए हर उबलता फ्लास्क ये वादा है कि गंभीर शोध भारतीय ज़मीन पर भी पनप सकता है।

panels.shot: intense close-up of Ray watching a reaction vessel, vapour rising softly
panels.action: Ray bends close over a reaction vessel held in tongs above a flame, faint vapours swirling as he peers through his spectacles, lips tightened in concentration.

dialogue.text: Night after night he systematically synthesizes and studies mercurous nitrite—an elusive compound—measuring, repeating, checking, until his tiny Calcutta room holds work fit for any European journal.

i18n.hi: रात दर रात वह पारे के नाइट्राइट को सधे तौर पर बनाता और परखता है—एक नाज़ुक यौगिक—मापता, दोहराता, जाँचता, जब तक कि उसका छोटा कलकत्ता वाला कमरा किसी भी यूरोपीय जर्नल के लायक काम से भर नहीं जाता।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Ray posting a thick envelope, street scene of colonial Calcutta behind
panels.action: On a bustling Calcutta street beside a red postbox, Ray slides a fat envelope marked for a foreign journal into the slot, trams and hand-pulled rickshaws moving in the background.

dialogue.text: In 1896 his careful study of mercurous nitrite leaves Calcutta for the wider world. From a colonial city’s back lane, a Bengali chemist quietly enters the international conversation.

i18n.hi: १८९६ में पारे के नाइट्राइट पर उसका बारीक अध्ययन कलकत्ता से निकल कर दुनिया तक पहुँचता है। एक औपनिवेशिक शहर की गली से, एक बंगाली रसायनज्ञ चुपचाप अंतरराष्ट्रीय चर्चा में दाखिल हो जाता है।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Ray lecturing in the lab, a small group of attentive students
panels.action: Back in the Presidency College laboratory, Ray stands beside a blackboard, chalk in hand, a few earnest students leaning forward as glassware gleams on the bench.

dialogue.text: Chemistry is not only to pass examinations. It must serve our people.

i18n.hi: रसायन सिर्फ़ इम्तिहान पास करने के लिए नहीं। इसे हमारे लोगों की सेवा करनी होगी।

panels.shot: wide shot juxtaposing a British-owned factory chimney with Ray walking past in thought
panels.action: Ray walks along the edge of the city, eyes lifted to the tall chimney of a British-owned chemical works belching smoke above rows of workers’ quarters.

dialogue.text: Around him, factories and pharmacies are mostly British-owned. Swadeshi is not yet a slogan, but he feels the imbalance: India buys medicines, does not make them.

i18n.hi: आसपास की ज़्यादातर फैक्ट्रियाँ और दवा की दुकानें ब्रिटिश मालिकों की हैं। स्वदेशी अभी नारा नहीं बना, पर उसे असंतुलन साफ़ दिखता है: भारत दवाएँ ख़रीदता है, बनाता नहीं।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot in his study, Ray reading an old Sanskrit manuscript beside modern chemistry texts
panels.action: Ray sits cross-legged on the floor, a palm-leaf Sanskrit manuscript open before him, thick Western chemistry volumes stacked nearby, his finger tracing a line of ancient script.

dialogue.text: He turns to Sanskrit treatises—Rasasastra, medical compendia—searching for India’s own chemical past. Could the land that once refined metals and medicines not also build modern laboratories?

i18n.hi: वह संस्कृत ग्रंथों की ओर लौटता है—रसशास्त्र, आयुर्वेदिक संहिताएँ—भारत के अपने रसायन इतिहास की खोज में। क्या जो ज़मीन कभी धातु और औषधियाँ साधती थी, वही आधुनिक लैब नहीं बना सकती?

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Ray drafting pages, a working title ‘History of Hindu Chemistry’ on the desk
panels.action: From behind his shoulder we see Ray writing on stacked sheets, diagrams and notes scattered around, a page bearing the words ‘History of Hindu Chemistry’ half-covered by his hand.

dialogue.text: Out of these readings grows his History of Hindu Chemistry. It is not nostalgia, but scholarship: evidence that Indians once practiced rigorous chemical arts, long before colonial rule.

i18n.hi: इन पढ़ाइयों से उसका ‘हिस्ट्री ऑफ़ हिंदू केमिस्ट्री’ जन्म लेता है। यह महज़ पुरानी याद नहीं, शोध है: सबूत कि भारतीयों ने सख़्त रासायनिक साधना कभी की थी, उपनिवेश से बहुत पहले।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Ray in the home lab speaking to a young visitor amid jars and mortars
panels.action: In his improvised laboratory, Ray stands amid shelves of labelled jars and grinding mortars, addressing a young visitor who listens wide-eyed in the doorway.

dialogue.speaker: prafulla_chandra_ray
dialogue.text: If we can prepare pure chemicals here, why should we depend on foreign firms?

i18n.hi: जब हम यहाँ शुद्ध रसायन बना सकते हैं, तो विदेशी कंपनियों पर क्यों निर्भर रहें?

panels.shot: wide shot of a slightly larger rented space, simple workers packing bottles under Ray’s supervision
panels.action: In a modest workshop room, a few workers in dhoti and shirts carefully fill and cork glass bottles as Ray supervises, ledger book open on a side table.

dialogue.text: By 1901, his idea takes shape as Bengal Chemical and Pharmaceutical Works. No grand building, only rented rooms—but inside, Indian hands prepare medicines and basic chemicals for sale.

i18n.hi: १९०१ तक उसका विचार आकार लेता है—बंगाल केमिकल एंड फ़ार्मास्यूटिकल वर्क्स। कोई शानो-शौकत नहीं, बस कुछ किराए के कमरे—पर भीतर, भारतीय हाथ दवा और ज़रूरी रसायन तैयार कर बाज़ार में उतारते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot, shelves lined with products, Ray in the foreground holding a labelled bottle
panels.action: Ray stands proudly inside the workshop, holding a freshly labelled bottle, behind him orderly shelves stacked with boxes and jars bearing Bengali and English markings.

dialogue.text: Bengal Chemical is both laboratory and enterprise. Its products compete against imports, and each invoice carries a quiet message: Indians can build scientific industry of their own.

i18n.hi: बंगाल केमिकल लैब भी है, कारोबार भी। उसके माल आयात से टक्कर लेते हैं, और हर बिल चुपचाप कहता है: भारतीय खुद भी वैज्ञानिक उद्योग खड़ा कर सकते हैं।

panels.shot: mid-shot in the Presidency lab, Ray guiding a young student at a bench
panels.action: In the college laboratory, Ray leans beside a young student at a bench, guiding his pipette hand, other students watching from behind.

dialogue.text: He does not keep chemistry locked in his company. At Presidency College, he trains students who will later be names like Meghnad Saha and S. N. Bose—future architects of Indian science.

i18n.hi: वह रसायन को अपनी कंपनी में कैद नहीं रखता। प्रेसीडेंसी कॉलेज में वह उन छात्रों को गढ़ता है जो आगे चलकर मेघनाद साहा और एस. एन. बोस जैसे नाम बनेंगे—भारतीय विज्ञान के भावी शिल्पी।

panels.shot: close-up of Ray’s thoughtful face as he looks from a scientific graph to a company ledger
panels.action: At his desk, Ray’s eyes move between a plotted experimental graph and an open ledger of Bengal Chemical’s accounts, his brows knit in concentrated balance.

dialogue.text: Research papers, company accounts, ancient manuscripts—he moves between them daily. For Ray, swadeshi is not armed revolt but the slow, disciplined weaving of knowledge into livelihoods.

i18n.hi: शोध-पत्र, कंपनी के खाते, प्राचीन पांडुलिपियाँ—वह रोज़ इन सबके बीच चलता है। राय के लिए स्वदेशी हथियार उठाना नहीं, बल्कि ज्ञान को रोज़गार में बुनने वाली धीमी, अनुशासित साधना है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a city pharmacy interior, Bengal Chemical products on the shelves among others
panels.action: Inside a Calcutta pharmacy, wooden shelves display rows of medicine bottles; among foreign labels, a line of Bengal Chemical products stands, a shopkeeper reaching for one.

dialogue.text: In time, Bengal Chemical’s bottles find their way onto shop shelves. They are ordinary items in ordinary lives, yet behind each one lies a choice to root modern science in Indian soil.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ बंगाल केमिकल की शीशियाँ दुकानों की रैक पर जगह पा लेती हैं। वे आम ज़िंदगियों की आम चीज़ें हैं, पर हर बोतल के पीछे ये फ़ैसला छिपा है कि आधुनिक विज्ञान को भारतीय मिट्टी में जड़ दी जाए।

panels.shot: mid-shot of an older Ray revising pages of his autobiography in a quiet room
panels.action: An older Ray, hair whiter, sits in a plain chair, spectacles low on his nose as he revises handwritten pages of his autobiography in a lamp-lit room.

dialogue.text: Later he will record it all in Life and Experiences of a Bengali Chemist—the training abroad, the struggles at home, the conviction that scholarship must touch work and welfare.

i18n.hi: बाद में वह सब कुछ ‘लाइफ़ एंड एक्सपीरियंसेज़ ऑफ़ अ बंगाली केमिस्ट’ में दर्ज करेगा—विदेश का प्रशिक्षण, घर की जद्दोजहद, और ये यक़ीन कि विद्वता को काम और कल्याण से जुड़ना ही होगा।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Ray seated in the lab, surrounded by students, workers, and stacks of books
panels.action: In a composite scene, Ray sits on a stool in the centre, behind him lab benches with students, to one side workers packing chemicals, to the other a pile of his scholarly volumes.

dialogue.text: He did not storm barricades or lead armies. Instead, Prafulla Chandra Ray showed another path to freedom: that a nation becomes strong when its learning creates medicines, work, and dignity for its people.

i18n.hi: उसने बैरिकेड नहीं तोड़े, न फ़ौजें चलाईं। बल्कि, प्रफुल्ल चंद्र राय ने आज़ादी की दूसरी राह दिखा दी: कि कोई राष्ट्र तब मज़बूत होता है जब उसका ज्ञान दवाएँ, काम और अपनी जनता की इज़्ज़त में बदल जाए।

title_i18n.en: The Chemist Who Made Swadeshi Medicine
